commits.message:
List the SDK declaration writer as a build step, not a generator

It writes only into the gitignored dist/, so the golden-channel table
ignores it like the core dist stamp.

Split the SDK into layer entry points and import them directly

The SDK root pulled every consumer onto the whole package, so one SDK
edit selected nearly every test. The SDK now has seven one-directional
layers (core, state-queue, da, operators, users, deployment,
fraud-proof); the root stays as the umbrella with the same exports.
Consumers import the layer they use. Files whose tests stub the root,
and files at their size cap, stay on the root and are baselined.

The layer entries are ESM-only so a CommonJS consumer cannot load two
copies of the SDK; the root keeps its CommonJS build. A module-graph
test pins each source file's owning layer.

Keep the hasher's members on the withdrawal-signature hash stub

The stub replaced blake2b with a bare function, so the multi-part hash
that core now computes with blake2b.create failed at module load.

Tell a file written during a test run by its own metadata, not a clock

The result cache took a file as written during a run when its times were at
or after a reading taken at the start. File times are not ordered against a
clock that is stepped: after a backward step, files written before the run
looked written during it and nothing was recorded, and a file edited and
restored during the run could look older than the start and be missed. The
snapshot now keeps each file's inode, size and nanosecond times as it reads
it, and a file whose metadata differs at the end was written.

Import fault-proofs and validation by subpath across packages

Other packages imported fault-proofs and validation through their root
entries, so an edit anywhere in either package selected every test that
used any part of it. Both packages now publish a subpath per cohesive unit
and importers use the one that declares the name. The root entries still
export everything. Files whose tests stub a name on the root, and the
node-tools pair that loads the compiled package at run time, stay on it.

WATCHER_PACKAGE_NAME moves to its own module so the watcher's CLI and
scaffold no longer reach each other for one constant.

A lint rule, midgard/no-cross-package-root, keeps it so.

Wait until the clock reaches the replay hold's retry time

The hold-runner test slept for the remaining time and then expected the held
event to be re-executed. A timer can fire a millisecond early, and the hold
is kept while the clock is before its retry time, so the run was sometimes
still held and all five tests of the file failed.

Import the module a file needs, not its package's index

Tests, test support and source modules in fault-proofs, watcher and node
imported through their own package's index modules, so nearly every test
depended on nearly the whole package and an edit to one module selected most
of the suite. They now import the defining module. Only import statements
change; names a test stubs on a module still come through that module.

A lint rule, midgard/no-own-package-barrel, keeps it so. The published
package entry points are unchanged.

Run the interactive-emulator test projects from the workspace bundle

The interactive-emulator projects of fault-proofs and watcher transformed
their source graph per file. They now load the workspace bundle, built with
the emulator-profile rewrite as a named source rewrite whose name, options
and code are part of the bundle key, so a plain and a rewritten bundle never
serve each other. Files the bundle analysis cannot serve stay on a
source-mode project.

Cut the test runner's per-run overhead and the node suite's setup time

contrib resolved a real path per input file and recomputed the preparation
plan four times a run, each prerequisite in its own identity scope. A
directory's real path is now resolved once per scope and the plan's
identities share one scope; the identities and the checks are unchanged.

The node suite's global setups move from the root config onto its projects,
so their workspace imports load from the bundle instead of being transformed
module by module, and the setup no longer rebuilds the native binary contrib
has just prepared for the same run.

Reset the paged verification fixture before its gated write

The fixture ran the application reset inside the follower-gated write, so the
gate was checked before the reset. A file run earlier on the same worker
database that left the gate at an applied view made the fixture's write
refused, and both paged tests failed depending on file order.

Bind the parsed fault-proof blueprint, not the raw one

The workflow deployment binding kept the raw blueprint JSON, so every
adapter and every direct-purpose transaction build parsed the whole
blueprint again: 9,063 parses and 24 s in the unused-script-witness
maximum-shape file, one per page-fit attempt. The binding and the
direct-purpose custody now hold the blueprint the resolver already
parses, typed so a raw blueprint cannot reach the build path. No cache is
added and nothing is accepted or refused differently.

Hash and encode the validation-trace replay with fewer copies

The replay spent about a third of its time on copies around hashing and
on re-encoding: Buffer.from, the generic CBOR encoder for the CEK machine
state, and a full witness encoding per step. Hash through libsodium's raw
export over one fixed heap region, hash multi-part input without joining
it, write the machine state's CBOR straight into one buffer, and build
each execution's core-step witness once with the step's state hash
dropped in. Every digest, encoded byte and refusal is unchanged, and any
value that is not a plain byte array still takes the previous path. The
maximum-shape builtin dispute file goes from about 280 s to about 190 s.

The hashed-byte counter the scaling gates use now binds libsodium's
export before wrapping it and refuses a run whose hook was replaced.

Resolve ledger descriptors once per retained deposit block build

The deposit-events block helper rebuilt the whole ledger root and
re-derived every entry's descriptor on each inserted deposit, 47 s of a
128 s inline-cap file. It now shares one descriptor resolver per block
build; roots and payloads are byte-identical. The nine inline-cap entries
in the duration table are scaled by the measured ratio.

Build the operator deployment once per run under the follower provider

Eight node files each built the same deployment through the follower
provider, about a minute apiece. The first file now builds it into a
run-shared fixture and every test starts from a fresh clone, so no file
depends on run order. operator-watchdog-emulator still builds its own, so
its stored-equals-confirmed check covers the deployment transactions in
every run, and each file's own check over what it submits is unchanged.
The duration table carries the measured ratios for those files and for
the frame-pressure file.

Find the frame-pressure payload sizes by estimate and bisection

Each target size took over twenty full payload builds to find. Start from
a one-probe estimate, widen and bisect, and build each target once per
mode for the cases that share it. The sizes found and both exact-size
checks are unchanged.
